contradictions: CLIENT TRANSPORT — QUIC vs raw TCP/UDP. client_arch and tests state the LIVE client (client/) speaks raw tokio TcpStream+UdpSocket to shards, while the project framing and shard_infra describe 'QUIC transport via quinn'. VERIFIED: client/src/net/{network.rs,connection.rs} use TcpStream/UdpSocket; quinn is NOT imported in client/src (grep for quinn/Endpoint in client/src returned nothing). RESOLUTION: inter-SHARD links are QUIC (shard-common/quic_transport.rs); client<->shard and client<->gateway are raw TCP+UDP. Both sets of agents are each half-right; the audit must treat 'client uses QUIC' as FALSE. This matters because a QUIC client rebuild requires server-side listener changes too.

GhostUpdate / source_demote grace — 'defined but unused' (handoff_path, churn) vs partially wired. VERIFIED: GhostUpdate has full serialize/deserialize round-trip in core/src/shard_message.rs (lines 685-703, 1638-1653, test at 2398) AND the CLIENT honors source_demote_after_ticks (client/src/net/network.rs:434 calls handle.demote(h.source_demote_after_ticks)). What is genuinely ABSENT is any SERVER-SIDE emit: grep for demote/Ghost across ship/system/planet/galaxy shards returns ZERO. So the correct statement is 'wire type + client consumer exist; no shard ever SENDS a GhostUpdate or honors the demote delay — the source despawns immediately.' shard_binaries/handoff_path's 'defined-but-unused' overstates; the precise gap is server-emit-only.

PERSISTENCE of block edits — 'only in-memory, shard crash loses everything' (shard_infra, handoff_path) vs partially persisted. VERIFIED: ship-shard/src/main.rs has load_grid_from_db (4646), save_block_configs (4570), load_block_configs (4510) backed by redb; planet-shard opens a redb (main.rs:3288-3294) but its OWN comments (2834-2840, 3288-3292) say it persists ONLY grants, 'doesn't yet persist block configs'. So persistence is real but uneven per shard-type, not a uniform absence. The agents' blanket 'in-memory only' is wrong for ship-shard, right for planet-shard.

INTER-SHARD AUTH — 'NO auth at all, PlayerHandoff spoofable' (shard_infra, handoff_path) vs a partial AuthorizedPeers layer exists. VERIFIED: shard-common/src/authorized_peers.rs exists and ship-shard gates SCENE/SEU data on it (main.rs:1125,1140,1628; planet-shard comment 743). HOWEVER the PlayerHandoff handler arm itself (ship-shard:1239, planet:718, system:863) does NOT call is_authorized — it trusts payload session_token/player_name/position directly. So 'PlayerHandoff is unauthenticated' is TRUE, but 'inter-shard QUIC has NO trust boundary whatsoever' is too strong: scene data has a HostSwitch-driven authorization filter. The transfer-control plane is unauthenticated; the scene-data plane is partially authorized.

gaps.gap: ACCOUNT / IDENTITY / SESSION-TOKEN model is entirely uncovered and is BROKEN as a security and correctness foundation. No agent analyzed how a player gets identity. VERIFIED: gateway mints session_token = SessionToken(rand_u64()) (gateway/src/main.rs:151) where rand_u64() (lines 193-201) hashes SystemTime::now() through std HashMap RandomState (SipHash) — NON-cryptographic, low-entropy, time-correlated. There is NO login, NO account, NO password/OAuth, NO token signature. Worse, NO shard ever validates that a presented session_token was minted by the gateway: client_listener.rs only stores tokens (session_observers map keyed by token) and never verifies them; the only validate_* functions in shards are spawn-mode arg checks (system-shard:1265). The session_token is simultaneously (a) the sole player identity, (b) the observer->client promotion key, and (c) the handoff correlation key. A guessable/forgeable token therefore = account takeover + handoff hijack + observer-promotion of an attacker's connection.
gaps.impact: DECISION-CRITICAL and REBUILD-FORCING. This is not a hardening item bolted onto either path: identity is the substrate the entire transfer state machine keys on. The eviction landmine, observer promotion, and handoff correlation all index on session_token. A transfer-first rebuild MUST define a real authenticated identity/session model (signed/opaque token minted at login, validated by every shard against orchestrator or via signature) BEFORE the transfer FSM, because the FSM's correctness invariants (exactly-one-authority, promote-the-right-connection) are meaningless if identity is forgeable. Strongly tilts toward rebuild-transfer-first with identity as milestone 0.
gaps.how_to_close: Already closed by direct verification: gateway/src/main.rs:151,193-201 (rand_u64 source); gateway/src/session.rs; shard-common/src/client_listener.rs (token stored never validated); grep confirmed no token validation in shards. To extend, read gateway/src/router.rs find_shard_for_player and types/src/shard.rs SessionToken to confirm there is no signature/expiry field.

gaps.gap: ORCHESTRATOR holds NO record of in-flight transfers, and universe_epoch_ms is not persisted — the control plane cannot recover an interrupted transfer and resets deterministic time on restart. handoff_path raised this as an open question; it is now answered and is larger than any agent treated it. VERIFIED: grep for transfer/handoff/in_flight/pending across orchestrator/src returns ZERO — redb stores only ShardInfo + LaunchConfig (persistence.rs:6-7). All transfer state lives in 4 process memories (pending_handoffs, PendingPlayerHandoffs, boarding_pending, session_observers). universe_epoch_ms = SystemTime::now() at orchestrator boot (main.rs:61-62, comment 'resets each dev cycle'), never persisted.
gaps.impact: ARCHITECTURAL, decision-critical. (a) A shard crash or orchestrator restart mid-transfer strands the player permanently (compounds the HandoffPending-never-removed bug — verified: zero remove::<HandoffPending> in repo). There is no authority that can roll a transfer back or forward. (b) universe_epoch_ms reset means after any orchestrator restart, every shard computes a DIFFERENT celestial_time, so all the position-reconstruction formulas (player_local = old_rot.inverse()*(pos-old_pos), ship-shard:1263-1267 etc.) that depend on synchronized orbital clocks silently drift — a whole class of 'transfer worked yesterday, broken today' bugs. This is the missing 'transfer coordinator/authority' the meshing_sota and saga patterns prescribe, and confirms keep-and-harden is NOT viable for the orchestration layer.
gaps.how_to_close: Verified via orchestrator/src/persistence.rs (only 2 tables) and orchestrator/src/main.rs:58-66 (epoch). To scope the fix, read orchestrator/src/registry.rs and lifecycle.rs to confirm there is no transfer-saga table, and decide whether the transfer coordinator lives in orchestrator (HTTP/redb) or as a new authority shard.

gaps.gap: PERSISTENCE / SAVE MODEL for the WORLD itself is largely unaddressed against the project's CENTRAL premise. The pitch is 'deterministic planets from seeds, no chunk streaming — only block-edit deltas networked.' That premise REQUIRES durable block-edit deltas, but VERIFIED: planet-shard explicitly does NOT persist block edits (main.rs:2834-2840 'planet-shard doesn't yet persist block configs ... inert until the player re-issues'); only ship-shard persists its grid (load_grid_from_db:4646). There is no edit-delta log, no per-planet delta store, no replay-on-rejoin path for planet surface edits. shard_binaries noted planet terrain collision is a flat halfspace but no agent connected the dots that the core networking model (delta-only) has no durable delta store for planets.
gaps.impact: ARCHITECTURAL and premise-invalidating if unaddressed. If planet block edits don't persist, the 'persistent voxel MMO' value prop doesn't hold — every shard restart wipes player builds on planets. This also interacts with transfers: a player who edits a planet, leaves via handoff, and returns finds their edits gone (planet redb has no edit table). The rebuild scope must include a durable, per-planet edit-delta store (the thing the marketing premise already promised) — this is foundational data architecture, not a transfer detail, and neither keep-vs-rebuild verdict accounted for its cost.
gaps.how_to_close: Read core/src/block/chunk_delta.rs and edit_pipeline.rs (the in-memory delta types), planet-shard/src/main.rs:377-3294 (confirms grants-only redb), and core/src/block/chunk_storage.rs to see if a serializable delta-log type exists that could be wired to redb. Confirm whether ship edits actually round-trip across restart via the load_grid_from_db path.

gaps.gap: PROTOCOL VERSIONING / WIRE COMPATIBILITY for ROLLING transfers is unanalyzed, despite being acute for a system where two shards on possibly-different binary versions exchange a handoff mid-rolling-upgrade. VERIFIED: the only version field is schema_version on the character_state BLOB (protocol/voxeldust.fbs:88; core/src/character/handoff_blob.rs SCHEMA_VERSION=2). There is NO wire-protocol version on client<->shard or shard<->shard messages, NO handshake negotiation, NO min-supported-version check. rust_netcode flagged FlatBuffers-vs-bitcode for the hot path but nobody examined cross-version handoff safety. quinn TLS uses self-signed skip-verify (quic_transport.rs:383) so there's also no ALPN/version pinning at the transport layer.
gaps.impact: MAJOR for operability of a live MMO. A handoff is precisely the moment two independently-deployed shards must agree on a wire format; without a negotiated version, a rolling deploy (or a stub-shard vs real-shard mix) silently mis-decodes PlayerHandoff's 12-Option god-struct, manifesting as 'random transfer breakage after deploy' — indistinguishable from the race bugs the user is already chasing. A transfer-first foundation needs an explicit per-message protocol version + negotiation. Medium decision-impact: doesn't force rebuild but is a mandatory item in either verdict and was missed.
gaps.how_to_close: Read protocol/voxeldust.fbs header tables and core/src/shard_message.rs serialize/deserialize entry points to confirm no top-level version field; check shard-common/src/quic_transport.rs for ALPN/version. Decision input for whether to keep FlatBuffers (schema-evolution-friendly) for control messages.

gaps.gap: FLOATING-ORIGIN / f64 PRECISION AT GALAXY SCALE is asserted as a strength on the client (origin.rs f64 ShardOrigin) but never validated end-to-end across the galaxy->system->planet->ship coordinate chain on the SERVER. VERIFIED: core/src/system.rs uses f64 throughout (G, sma, anomalies) and the wire types use Vec3d/Quatd (f64). But no agent checked whether SYSTEM-space and GALAXY-space absolute coordinates stay within f64 precision at real interstellar distances, nor whether the per-shard rebase actually re-origins server-side (client origin.rs rebases, but shards appear to simulate in their own local frames with hand-matched reconstruction formulas, handoff_path:coordinate-duplication). The reconstruction formulas depend on synchronized orbital clocks which (per gap above) reset on orchestrator restart.
gaps.impact: MAJOR, latent. 'Star Citizen scale' is a stated goal; SC itself needed 64-bit zone-relative coords precisely because f32 world coords shatter past ~16km and f64 single-origin still degrades at AU/light-year scale. If server shards carry absolute f64 positions without a per-zone origin, depenetration/hull-trap math and transfer pose reconstruction lose precision exactly at the boundaries where transfers happen. Medium-high decision-impact: a transfer-first rebuild must fix the coordinate-frame story (one tested cross-frame primitive, per handoff_path) and that decision needs a precision budget no agent produced.
gaps.how_to_close: Read core/src/spatial.rs and core/src/planet_rotation.rs (coords) for the frame definitions; read the 4 reconstruction sites (ship-shard:1263-1273, system:2135-2142/2354-2366, planet:1243-1263) to quantify whether they operate in a re-origined local frame or absolute system space. Compute worst-case f64 ULP at max system radius to set a precision budget.

gaps.gap: The 'EVA stuck — can't move but camera rotates' symptom (the user's hallmark bug) is attributed to TWO different root causes by different agents, and neither was traced to a single confirmed mechanism. shard_binaries blames the UDP-to-session IP-matching heuristic (discover_udp leaving udp_addr=None -> all PlayerInput silently dropped). handoff_path blames the same IP-match plus secondary-eviction dropping the to-be-promoted connection. client_arch blames raw-TCP/UDP redundant-forwarding races. These may all contribute, but the audit needs ONE confirmed causal chain to know if it's fixable in place or needs the connection-ownership redesign.
gaps.impact: DECISION-CRITICAL because it is the user's primary pain and the meshing_sota research says the FIX is structural (gateway-owns-connection so the client socket never re-homes). If the stuck-bug is fundamentally the client-re-homes-its-own-connection model (observer pre-connect + promote), that validates rebuild-transfer-first with a connection-owning edge; if it's merely the IP-match heuristic, it's a targeted fix. The two have very different scope.
gaps.how_to_close: Read shard-common/src/client_listener.rs discover_udp / session_for_udp / promote_observer_to_client (around lines 200-410) to confirm the udp_addr=None-after-promote path; cross-check client/src/net/connection.rs:550-585 session-token retag-on-promote. This single read pair determines whether the stuck-bug is heuristic (patchable) or architectural (connection re-homing).

gaps.gap: DENIAL-OF-SERVICE / RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION surface of the unauthenticated transfer plane is unconsidered. Given verified findings (no token validation, fire-and-forget try_send handoffs, session_observers map with NO eviction/staleness sweep per handoff_path, HandoffPending never removed), an attacker or even a buggy client can register unbounded session_observers, spoof PlayerHandoff to spawn ghost players, or wedge entities. No agent assessed abuse/DoS.
gaps.impact: MAJOR for a multiplayer MMO but LOWER decision-impact for keep-vs-rebuild (it's a consequence of the identity gap above). It reinforces that the transfer plane needs auth + bounded resources, which both verdicts already imply. Listed so the orchestrating model doesn't treat security as solely the cert layer.
gaps.how_to_close: Read shard-common/src/client_listener.rs session_observers lifecycle (register/unregister/promote, lines ~200-410) to confirm no cap/TTL; read the PlayerHandoff arms (ship:1239, planet:718, system:863) to confirm no rate-limit/auth. Already partially verified.

gaps.gap: WARP (galaxy<->system) — the 4th transition class — is the least-traced transfer path; handoff_path explicitly could not follow its source-side emit. This couples the transfer FSM to the provisioner lifecycle, which is exactly where a transfer-first rebuild must define 'await-provision-or-rollback' semantics. Medium-high decision-impact: it's the case that most needs the orchestrator-as-transfer-authority design.
gaps.how_to_close: Read system-shard/src/main.rs:4500-4520 (galaxy handoff emit) and galaxy-shard/src/main.rs drain_provisions + warp arrival handler; read system-shard:1907-1945 to confirm the 'dest not provisioned -> warn and drop' path.
